$comment: The zero-downtime swap. The health gate is the whole point - traffic never moves until the new colour answers.
image_prompt: Draw a UML sequence diagram with five participants: 'GitHub Actions runner', 'EC2 host (docker)', 'rideiq-green (NEW)', 'nginx', 'rideiq-blue (OLD)'. Number every message. Show: pull the image, start the new colour with no published port, then a labelled loop fragment 'poll /health, up to 30 times, 2 s apart' against the new colour. Then a decision: draw a red alt fragment labelled 'never became healthy' containing 'remove the new container, leave nginx untouched, fail the deploy - the old colour keeps serving', and a green alt labelled 'healthy' containing 'rewrite nginx upstream to the new colour', 'nginx -s reload', 'drain 30 s', 'remove the old container'. Emphasise visually that traffic only moves AFTER the health check passes.

style.look: clean UML-style sequence diagram, flat modern, generous vertical spacing
conventions: Participants across the top as labelled boxes with vertical dashed lifelines.
Solid arrow = request. Dashed arrow = response.
Self-call drawn as a small loop back onto the same lifeline.
Number every message so the reading order is unambiguous.
Draw alt / opt fragments as a labelled rectangle spanning the lifelines involved.

messages.label: SSH in with the deploy key
decide which colour is live; the other one becomes the target
docker run - no published port, joined to appnet
200 once the 16 ML models have finished training
write the new upstream config and reload
wait 30 s to drain, then docker rm -f

fragments.label: poll /health up to 30 times, 2 s apart (~60 s budget)
fragments.note: the app trains 16 ML models on boot, so a slow start is normal, not a failure

fragments.label: never became healthy
fragments.note: remove the new container, leave nginx pointing at the old colour, fail the deploy. Zero downtime because traffic never moved.

annotations: Traffic only moves AFTER the new colour answers /health. That single ordering is what makes the deploy safe.
The old colour is not deleted immediately - it drains for 30 seconds so in-flight requests finish.
Redis is started once and never swapped, so the cache survives every deploy.
A rollback is the same dance with an older SHA: workflow_dispatch with rollback_sha skips the build and the CI gate entirely.
